# Quill

> Quill is a small, general-purpose programming language with classes, exceptions, closures, a module system, and its own web server. Python-style indentation, dynamically typed, implemented as a tree-walking interpreter (reference build in Python; a separate Rust port exists with no Python runtime required).

Quill uses `pull` for function definitions instead of `def`/`fn`, and real f-strings: `f"hi {name}"` interpolates, plain `"hi {name}"` never does.

## Install

Not published to PyPI yet. Clone the repo and install from source:

```
git clone https://github.com/riadworks/quill-lang.git
cd quill-lang
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\pip install -e .
```

Source: https://github.com/riadworks/quill-lang

This provides a `quill` command: run with no arguments for a REPL, or `quill script.ql` to run a file.

## What's implemented

- Classes with single inheritance, `super.method()` resolving correctly through deep chains
- Exceptions: `try` / `except` / `finally`, catching both user `raise`s and built-in runtime errors
- Closures and first-class functions
- A module system (`import "file.ql" as name`)
- Operator overloading via dunder methods (`__add__`, `__eq__`, `__str__`, etc.)
- List/map comprehensions and destructuring assignment
- A built-in web server (`serve(port, handler)`) and an outbound HTTP client (`http_get`/`http_post`)
- A standard library covering strings, lists, maps, JSON, SHA-256, randomness, and file I/O

## What's not implemented

Multiple inheritance, reflected operators (`__radd__`-style), a package manager, async/concurrency, and static typing.

## Real programs built with it

A persistent CLI task manager, the same task manager as a website with a JSON API, a URL shortener, a text adventure, a password generator, and a number-guessing game - all shipped with the project's source.
